sources.title: Personal biography: birth year, education, business background, party entry and municipal election/inauguration dates
sources.findings: Read the official personal biography. It supports birth in Akçaabat in 1970; use the year only because the exact day/month was not independently verified in this review. It records 1992 family-business work, a 1994 Istanbul business-administration graduation, later master’s study, 2008 CHP entry, the 2014 district election, 17 April 2019 assumption of office, 6 May annulment, 23 June rerun and 27 June return. Education, ongoing service and party language are historical and must be qualified by later cancellations, suspension and the 2026 party change. Its June 2024 municipal-union presidency is not automatically a current office. Positive municipal-impact claims are not independently evaluated here.

sources.title: Historical mayor biography: district service, family business, sports administration and 2019 elections
sources.findings: Read İETT’s historical biography. It corroborates the 1970 birthplace, municipal career, family construction business and sports-club administration. Do not convert amateur football or club-board service into a professional football career. Its statement that he was a graduate student in 1992 is inconsistent with the separately supported 1994 undergraduate completion, and its 2009 CHP entry differs from the personal biography and Reuters’s 2008; those inconsistent details are not copied. The page’s current mayor and degree wording is outdated. District mayor and citywide metropolitan mayor are different posts, and praise for local projects is institutional assessment rather than measured causal evidence.

sources.title: 1 April 2024 report of 31 March local elections: Istanbul re-election and 2019 end to 25 years of AKP/predecessor rule
sources.findings: Read Reuters’s report dated 1 April about the 31 March 2024 local vote. It confirms re-election against Murat Kurum and the 2019 end of roughly 25 years of rule by the AKP and its predecessors, not 25 years by the AKP alone. Its figures were partial returns, not final certified percentages. National prominence and analysts’ predictions do not establish a presidential victory or eligibility. The presidential election in 2023 is a separate contest.

sources.title: 18 March 2025: university cancellation statement and İmamoğlu’s rejection of its legality
sources.findings: Read DHA’s 18 March 2025 reproduction of the university statement and İmamoğlu’s response. The decision annulled transfer decisions and related qualifications/diplomas for 28 graduates over alleged defects in 1990 transfers. This is an administrative university action, not a criminal forgery judgment. He disputed the board’s legal authority; that objection is his position, not a reversal already obtained. The original university decision and complete underlying investigation were not independently inspected. Do not describe 38 graduates as losing diplomas: the statement distinguishes 10 deregistered people from the 28 graduates.

sources.title: 28 July 2025 report: master’s qualification cancelled by the institute on 24 July
sources.findings: Read Anadolu’s 28 July 2025 report. The institute board’s master’s cancellation decision was taken on 24 July, following the earlier undergraduate annulment and its prerequisite implications. Distinguish decision and publication dates, undergraduate versus postgraduate decisions, and database removal from the underlying administrative act. The report’s discussion of a forgery indictment and possible sentence concerns allegations and prosecution, not a conviction. No underlying thesis, transcript or board minutes were inspected.

sources.title: 23 January 2026: administrative court rejects challenge to undergraduate diploma cancellation
sources.findings: Read Anadolu’s 23 January 2026 account of the fifth administrative court’s rejection of the diploma challenge. The quoted reasoning concerns transfer rules, quotas and the university’s power to withdraw an erroneous administrative act. This is administrative litigation, not the separate criminal forgery prosecution. The dossier records the rejection without treating the news date as a verified original judgment-signature date or claiming every possible appeal had ended.

sources.title: 6 March 2026: regional administrative chamber rejects a request to suspend execution
sources.findings: Read DW/ANKA’s 6 March 2026 article. Its detailed body specifies that the regional seventh administrative chamber rejected a request for suspension of execution; the broader headline must not be read as final exhaustion of the merits appeal. It also compresses 19 March custody, later remand and suspension into a single narrative; use the separately verified 23 March remand/suspension date. The report notes a university qualification requirement for presidential candidacy, but it is not a current electoral commission ruling registering or rejecting a future nomination.

sources.title: 23 March 2025: Interior Ministry statement on remand and temporary suspension from office
sources.findings: Read DHA’s 23 March 2025 account quoting the Interior Ministry. It identifies the judicial remand order that day and a temporary suspension under Constitution article 127 and Municipal Law article 47. Administrative suspension is neither a final corruption conviction nor a finding that every alleged offence occurred. The same article discusses two district mayors: the terrorism allegation and appointed trustee for Şişli are not attributed to İmamoğlu or to Istanbul’s metropolitan municipality. The original social-media ministry statement and court order were not separately inspected.

sources.title: 13 August 2026: resignation statement issued on 12 August and support for Yeni Parti
sources.findings: Read Euronews’s 13 August 2026 report, which dates the resignation statement to 12 August. It records departure from the CHP and support for the Özgür Özel-led Yeni Parti, continued detention, denials of corruption and the earlier 23 March 2025 CHP primary. The quoted 17-year membership duration is not harmonised with the independently supported 2008 entry date; omit the duration. Resignation, support and later confirmed membership are separate. Party-reported primary/solidarity-ballot participation is not independently certified, so no turnout total is used. Party designation is not legal registration for the next presidential election.

sources.title: 14 August 2026: provincial party chair confirms İmamoğlu’s membership of Yeni Parti
sources.findings: Read Habertürk’s 14 August 2026 ANKA report quoting provincial leader Özgür Çelik’s confirmation that İmamoğlu had become Yeni Parti’s first member in Istanbul. This supports completed membership rather than mere intent to join. The article’s publication date is not necessarily the exact registration date. Neither the first-member description nor presidential-candidate wording makes him party chair or confirms statutory presidential eligibility. The record does not rely on unofficial party-fan chronology pages with conflicting dates.

sources.title: 2 November 2026: new stage of municipal corruption proceedings following the 17 October defence
sources.findings: Read Hürriyet Daily News’s 2 November 2026 account of the corruption trial’s new witness stage after his 17 October defence. It records ongoing imprisonment and his contention that the case was political. The release of seven other defendants is not his release. Proposed questioning of witnesses, future evidence examination and a future prosecution opinion are not all completed events. A historical December 2025 statement is introduced with the speaker’s current New Party title; do not infer the new party already existed in December 2025. Do not present this phase as only the third day of the entire lengthy trial.

sources.title: 9 November 2026 report: testimony phase resumed on 2 November and İmamoğlu’s recent defence
sources.findings: Read Medyascope’s article published 9 November 2026, explicitly dating the resumed hearing to 2 November and the close of his four-day defence to 17 October. Its later uses of today are not grounds to redate the hearing to the article’s publication day. It reports his actual recent defence, denials and continued pre-trial detention. Witness allegations about other defendants are not attributed as proven personal acts by him. No attached video or full trial transcript was viewed. Statements about a politically motivated process remain attributed, not a judicial acquittal.

sources.title: 3 November 2026 publication of third-party intervention concerning pre-trial detention before the European Court of Human Rights
sources.findings: Read the opening and relevant context of the HRW-published third-party intervention dated 3 November 2026, not every cited authority. It concerns pre-trial detention, records custody from 19 March and suspension on 23 March, and advances human-rights arguments about judicial independence. Leave to intervene is not a merits victory, release order or ECtHR judgment for him. The opening’s CHP affiliation describes the earlier context and is not used to override the verified August 2026 party change. Judgments cited concerning Kavala, Demirtaş and others are not judgments in İmamoğlu’s own case.

sources.title: 11 November 2026: separate party-congress criminal case adjourned without a verdict to 18 November
sources.findings: Read Gazete Kritik’s 11 November 2026 report of the separate CHP congress criminal proceedings before the Ankara 26th criminal court. The hearing ended with an adjournment to 18 November and no merits verdict. Prosecutorial requests for sentences of one to three years for nine defendants are not imposed sentences; acquittal requests for three others are not completed acquittals. The underlying congress was on 4–5 November 2023. This criminal case differs from both the municipal corruption case and the civil litigation about the party congress. Defences delivered by Erkan Aydın and Baki Aydöner are not treated as a new personal appearance by İmamoğlu.

sources.title: 17 November 2026 preview of party-congress hearing: prosecution requests and possible ruling are not a verdict
sources.findings: Read Haber Ekspres’s 17 November 2026 preview of the next day’s party-congress hearing. A possible ruling is an expectation, not an observed judgment; no 18 November outcome was verified in this review. It distinguishes prosecution submissions from verdicts and the separate civil congress case from criminal liability. The article contains malformed spellings or stray words in some other defendants’ names; those lists are not reproduced. Political-ban possibilities discussed by commentators are not final orders imposed in this case.

sources.title: 31 March–1 April 2024 profile: 1994 graduation, 2008 party entry and repeated municipal victories
sources.findings: Read Reuters’s profile on Investing.com, dated 31 March and updated 1 April 2024. It corroborates birth year 1970, 1994 business-administration graduation, 2008 CHP entry, district leadership and successive Istanbul victories. It provides historical context only: old degree status, CHP membership and pending appeal descriptions are not automatically current. Its forecast of a future presidency is not a fact. Its discussion of an earlier insult conviction also means that describing the current corruption proceedings as unresolved must not be broadened into a claim that he has never been convicted in any separate case. A shortened reference to court annulment is clarified by the official chronology identifying the YSK.
